title: Custom payment methods — MPP documentation
quote: The `mppx` SDK allows dynamic extensibility for custom payment methods integrating any payment rail—blockchains, card processors, or proprietary systems. A custom payment method requires three components: Method definition using `Method.from()`, Client logic for creating Credentials on 402 responses, Server logic for verification and Receipt generation.

title: The 'Payment' HTTP Authentication Scheme (draft-httpauth-payment-00)
quote: payment-method-id = 1*LOWERALPHA ; LOWERALPHA = %x61-7A ; a-z. intent-token = 1*( ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" ). §11.3 Replay Protection: Payment methods used with this specification MUST provide single-use proof semantics. A payment proof MUST be usable exactly once; subsequent attempts to use the same proof MUST be rejected by the payment method infrastructure.

title: mpp-specs — core draft: IANA Payment Method Registry
quote: This document establishes the "HTTP Payment Methods" registry. This registry uses the "Specification Required" policy defined in {{RFC8126}}. Registration requests must include: Method Identifier: Unique lowercase ASCII letters (`a-z`); Description; Specification pointer; Registrant Contact. The registry is initially empty.

title: mpp-specs — CONTRIBUTING: adding a new method or intent

title: MPP (Machine Payments Protocol) — Cloudflare Agents documentation
quote: MPP is payment-method agnostic. It supports stablecoins, cards through Stripe, and custom payment methods. A service can offer more than one method.

title: MPP Explained: The Machine Payments Protocol
quote: MPP was co-authored by Stripe and Tempo and launched on 18 March 2026. It is published as an open standard, with the specification at mpp.dev.

title: Protocol overview — MPP documentation
quote: New payment methods can be defined by any implementer. Each method must specify: Method identifier (unique lowercase ASCII string); Request schema; Payload schema; Verification procedure; Settlement procedure. Parameters MUST use lowercase names; clients ignore unknown parameters.

title: Machine Payments Protocol — overview
quote: Works with stablecoins, cards, and bank transfers—All payment methods can be supported through one protocol. Built on an open specification proposed to the IETF. A flexible core allows advanced flows like disputes or additional primitives like identity to be gradually introduced.

title: Service Discovery for HTTP Payment Authentication (draft-payment-discovery-00)
quote: Services publish an OpenAPI document annotated with payment extensions that describe pricing, payment methods, and intent types. The runtime 402 challenge remains authoritative for all payment parameters.

title: mpp-specs — repository structure (core / intents / methods / extensions)
quote: Core (specs/core/): HTTP 402 semantics, headers, IANA registries. Intents (specs/intents/): abstract payment patterns such as charge, authorize, and subscription. Methods (specs/methods/): concrete implementations for specific networks. Extensions (specs/extensions/): optional protocol additions, such as discovery and identity.

title: Method.toServer — MPP TypeScript SDK API reference
quote: Documented options: broadcast, canOffer, defaults, request, respond, transport, validate, verify (deprecated). broadcast: "Completes payment and returns its Receipt. Revalidate any external or on-chain state before the terminal operation, because a previous `validate` result is advisory." validate: "Validates a Credential without settling, reserving, broadcasting, or otherwise consuming payment state." verify: "Legacy combined validation and settlement function. Use `validate` and `broadcast` for new methods."

title: mppx — src/Store.ts (store interface and built-in constructors)
quote: Async key-value store interface. Modeled after Cloudflare KV's API (`get`/`put`/`delete`). Atomic read-modify-write for a single key: `fn` receives the current value (or `null`) and returns a Change describing the write to perform. Module exports observed in mppx 0.8.15: cloudflare, from, memory, redis, upstash.
